question.problem:
Evaluate ${f}_{xyz}(4,1,7)$ given that a function $f(x,y,z)$ and all of its higher-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U,$ and that

$$
{f}_{xz}(x,y,z)=2x\sqrt{z-3y}+z{e}^{x-4y}
$$
question.worked_solution:
As the higher-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U,$ the mixed partial derivatives must be equal. 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xyz}(x,y,z) & ={f}_{xzy}(x,y,z) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{xz}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x\sqrt{z-3y}+z{e}^{x-4y}) \\  & =2x\cdot (-\frac{3}{2\sqrt{z-3y}})-4z{e}^{x-4y} \\  & =-\frac{3x}{\sqrt{z-3y}}-4z{e}^{x-4y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point  $(4,1,7):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xyz}(4,1,7) & =-\frac{3\cdot 4}{\sqrt{7-3\cdot 1}}-4\cdot 7\cdot {e}^{4-4\cdot 1} \\  & =-\frac{12}{\sqrt{7-3}}-28{e}^{4-4} \\  & =-6-28 \\  & =-34\end{aligned}
$$
